summary: Fairfield County fire tower listed under the South Carolina Forestry Commission and marked removed; no other detail found in the sources checked.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed on the eastern U.S. lookouts site; no removal date found.

evidence.supports: Tower is listed in Fairfield County
Listed under the South Carolina Forestry Commission
Eastern lookouts record marks the tower as removed
Towers were the public's fire reporting point and the link to firefighters in the field
evidence.quote: Towers were the public's fire reporting contact point, and served as the communications link for firefighters in the field.

evidence.supports: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993
evidence.quote: The Forestry Commission closed its fire tower system on October 1, 1993.

notes_for_editor: Thinnest of the three. The eastern lookouts page has only a title, county, agency and a removed label; no build date, design, height, staffing or site description. The story is short (under the 120-word floor) because the evidence is that thin; the statewide context paragraph is labeled as statewide and is not a claim about this tower. Search results were not useful. Two leads were seen only as search snippets and are not used: a Fire Tower Circle address in Jenkinsville (a recycling center listing on recyclefind.com) and a Fire Tower Rd county property record. Neither is tied to the tower by any source read. Neither the NHLR nor the FFLOS registers in the cache list this site. The FFLA South Carolina page (Ron Kemnow notes) was not readable from the cache.
